Greptile Summary

This PR introduces three GitHub Actions workflows (`release.yml`, `nightly.yml`, `beta.yml`) that build, sign, and publish Tuari desktop artifacts across stable, beta, and nightly channels, along with a post-build smoke test script and its test suite. - **Workflows**: All three follow the same structure — setup, architecture guardrail check, Tauri build, Ed25519 signing with optional production key fallback, smoke test, artifact staging, and GitHub Release upload. The nightly now reads its base version from `tauri.conf.json` rather than a hardcoded string. - **Signing**: Each workflow writes the signature into `updates.json` and conditionally selects the public key for smoke testing based on whether `UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY` is set. However, `--key-id "dev-key-v1"` is hardcoded in all three workflows, so every signed manifest — including production ones — permanently embeds the dev key identifier in the signed payload. - **Smoke test (`verify-release-assets.mjs`)**: Checks that the portable zip contains `Tuari.exe` and that the `.update` package signature is cryptographically valid, but the `--version` and `--channel` arguments that are passed by all three workflows are parsed and then silently ignored — no cross-check of the artifact's embedded metadata against expected values is performed.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The workflows are functional for the dev-key path but have two defects that will surface once production secrets are fully wired up. Every signed update package — including production stable releases — will permanently embed keyId: 'dev-key-v1' in its signed payload because the flag is hardcoded. When a production key rotation occurs, there will be no way to distinguish old from new keys from the manifest alone. Separately, the smoke test accepts --version and --channel arguments from all three workflows but never acts on them, so a mis-tagged artifact would silently pass verification. Both defects are present in all three newly-added workflows. .github/workflows/release.yml, .github/workflows/nightly.yml, .github/workflows/beta.yml (hardcoded key-id); scripts/verify-release-assets.mjs (unused version/channel args).

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | .github/workflows/release.yml | Stable release workflow — correctly reads version from tag, properly constructs updates.json with actual signature, and conditionally selects the right public key for smoke testing. Hardcodes --key-id "dev-key-v1" even when the production signing key is used. | | .github/workflows/nightly.yml | Nightly workflow — version now correctly read from tauri.conf.json. Same --key-id "dev-key-v1" hardcoding issue as release.yml and beta.yml. | | .github/workflows/beta.yml | Beta workflow triggered by manual dispatch with version input. Mirrors nightly/release structure; shares the same --key-id "dev-key-v1" hardcoding issue. | | scripts/verify-release-assets.mjs | Post-build smoke test: verifies portable zip contains Tuari.exe and validates the Ed25519 signature on the .update package. Accepts --version and --channel CLI args but never acts on them, so channel/version cross-checking is absent. | | tests/verify-release-assets.test.mjs | 7-test suite for the smoke test script; cross-platform zip creation now uses zip on Unix and PowerShell on Windows. Tests cover missing artifacts, tampered update packages, and the full happy-path flow. | | scripts/sign-update.mjs | Unchanged signing script; correctly uses canonical JSON and Ed25519. The --key-id option injects the value into the signed payload, which is why hardcoding it in the workflows is impactful. | | tests/workflow-assets.test.mjs | New test validates that all three CI/CD workflow files exist and contain expected triggers, environments, and referenced scripts. Provides a lightweight structural guard against accidental workflow breakage. |

Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 1 code review issue. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 .github/workflows/release.yml:170-174 **`--key-id` is always `"dev-key-v1"` even with the production key** `--key-id "dev-key-v1"` is hardcoded in all three workflows, so the `keyId` field embedded in the signed canonical JSON will read `"dev-key-v1"` even when the production secret `UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY` is used. The key-id is part of the signed bytes (`sign-update.mjs` line 153: `manifestObj.keyId = keyId`), meaning every production artifact is permanently mislabeled. Any client or auditing tool that inspects the keyId to select the right verification key or to enforce key-rotation policy will behave incorrectly — it cannot distinguish a dev-signed nightly from a production-signed stable release. The same hardcoded value appears in `nightly.yml` line 162 and `beta.yml` line 160. `````
